claims.text: Polycrystalline metals and alloys exhibit temperature-dependent plastic deformation.
Ti-6Al-4V is a suitable material for studying temperature-dependent plastic deformation.
Temperature-dependent plastic deformation in Ti-6Al-4V is caused by thermally activated dislocation glide.
Temperature-dependent plastic deformation in Ti-6Al-4V is caused by grain-boundary sliding.
In-situ TEM can be used to study the proposed temperature-dependent deformation behavior.
In-situ XRD can be used to study the proposed temperature-dependent deformation behavior.
The proposed initial material is polycrystalline Ti-6Al-4V with an average grain size of 10 μm.
The proposed intervention is uniaxial tensile deformation at 25°C, 200°C, and 400°C.
The proposed tensile strain rate is 10^-3 s^-1.
Dislocation density is a structural mediator of the temperature-dependent response.
Grain-boundary structure is a structural mediator of the temperature-dependent response.
Plastic strain at 400°C will be 30% greater than at 25°C.
Yield strength at 400°C will be 20% lower than at 25°C.
The applicable temperature range is 25°C to 400°C.
The magnitude of temperature-dependent deformation may vary with material composition.
The magnitude of temperature-dependent deformation may vary with microstructure.

contradictions.description: The predicted 20% yield-strength decrease corresponds to a 400°C strength exactly equal to 80% of the 25°C value, but the falsification rule rejects any result that is not less than 80%, including the predicted value of exactly 80%.
